extracted.intended_audience: publishers, literary journal editors and institutions submitting short stories on behalf of authors (and authors preparing submissions for the Caine Prize)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and eligibility criteria for submitting short stories to the 2026 Caine Prize for African Writing, aimed at publishers or third-party institutions submitting on behalf of authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication date window
rubrics_metrics.description: The story must have been published in the five years preceding the submissions deadline. For 2026 eligibility, the judges will only consider work published between 27 February 2021 and 27 February 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only stories published within the specified date range are eligible; publication date is a strict criterion for 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word count limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries must be between 3,000 and 10,000 words in length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short stories shorter than 3,000 words or longer than 10,000 words are not eligible for the Prize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may submit (publisher/third-party requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries must be submitted by a publisher. This includes publishers of physical and digital books, literary journals, magazines, and arts-oriented websites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries submitted by the author themselves are ineligible; submissions must come from a publisher or a third-party institution independent of the author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher cannot be the author
rubrics_metrics.description: Kindly note that the publisher submitting the entry cannot also be the author of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflict-of-interest rule: the submitting publisher must be distinct from the author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author age requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers must be over 18 years of age at the time of submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors under 18 are ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: No self-published or unpublished works
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-published and unpublished short stories are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For avoidance of doubt, stories self-published on self-publishing platforms – WattPad, author-me.com, Lulu and Amazon Kindle, or similar – are not eligible for the Prize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple submissions by publishers
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers are encouraged to submit multiple short stories as long as they do not submit more than one story by the same author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The judges will only consider one work per writer in any given year. If separate publishers submit different stories by the same author, the organisers will contact the writer to choose which story to put forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-time entry per story (no re-submission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories may only be entered for consideration for The Caine Prize for African Writing once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may not re-submit a story for consideration, even if it was not selected for the shortlist; you are encouraged to submit a different story that meets eligibility criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible genres and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Genres not eligible for entry include: novels, children’s stories, factual writing, academic essays, plays, poetry, autobiography/biography, and any work that does not constitute a fictional short story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only fictional short stories are eligible; explicit list of excluded types clarifies borderline cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Must specify author's African country and word count
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must specify which African country the author comes from and the short story word count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required metadata for each submission; omission may make the submission ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher must obtain author's consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers must obtain the consent of the author before submitting the short story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consent is a precondition for submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital submission format / PDF requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting digitally published short stories, kindly provide a PDF version. Alternatively, you may instead provide a PDF containing a link to the publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organisers accept digital submissions but require a PDF (or a PDF with link) to ensure stable access to the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit multiple entries (email + application letters)
rubrics_metrics.description: If submitting multiple stories for consideration, please send your entries via email to submissions@caineprize.com, including an Application Letter that contains all the information requested in the submission form for each story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All submissions must comply with the rules of entry and include the required information outlined in the submission form to be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility support / queries
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have any doubt whether your work is eligible, please send an email to submissions@caineprize.com, and we will be happy to assist you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organisers provide direct support to clarify borderline eligibility questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'African writer'
rubrics_metrics.description: An ‘African writer’ is taken to mean someone who is a national of an African country, or who has a parent who is African by birth or nationality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility of an author is determined by nationality or parentage as stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission window / deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions for The Caine Prize for African Writing open on Monday, 1 December 2025 (00:01 GMT) and close on Friday, 6 March 2026 (23:59 GMT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries must be submitted within these dates and times (GMT).

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations eligibility and prize split
rubrics_metrics.description: Works translated into English from other languages are eligible, provided they have been published in English translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such a work wins, the prize pot is split between the translator and the original language author as follows: 70% of the prize pot to the author, and 30% to the translator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author must be alive at time of submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Can I submit stories by writers who have passed away? No. Authors should be alive at the time their stories are submitted for the Prize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posthumous submissions are explicitly disallowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions if shortlisted (reproduction & distribution rights)
rubrics_metrics.description: By submitting an entry to the Prize, the publisher and author agree that, if the work is shortlisted, the Caine Prize will retain a perpetual, non-exclusive right to reproduce and distribute the story in its anthologies and related materials, including in digital, audio, and audiovisual formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shortlisting implies grant of reproduction/distribution rights for anthologies and related materials; rights are perpetual but non-exclusive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions if shortlisted (excerpts for marketing)
rubrics_metrics.description: By submitting an entry to the Prize, the publisher and author agree that, if the story is shortlisted, the Prize is granted permission to publish excerpts of the short story for marketing and promotional purposes. The author will always be credited for any publication or reproduced extract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organisers will use excerpts for promotion but commit to crediting the author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortlist participation expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The winner and shortlisted writers will be invited to participate in online and in-person events should resources and circumstances permit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By consenting to submission, shortlisted writers agree to take part in Prize related events (panels, interviews, readings, podcasts) and will receive a separate letter detailing terms of agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance condition for acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Please note that all submissions must comply with the rules of entry and include the required information outlined in the submission form to be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions that do not meet the stated criteria and required information will not be eligible for the Prize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of e-books/digital versions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you accept e-books or digital versions of entries? Yes. We accept digital submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Digital publications are acceptable provided they meet other eligibility and format requirements (PDF or PDF with link preferred).
